an1.248:1.1: They were merchants from Ukkalā (modern Odisha on the Bay of Bengal) who offered the first meal to the Buddha after his awakening ([pli-tv-kd1:4.2.1]()). Their spiritual attainments are noted at [an6.119]()–20. Tapussa also appears at [an9.41]().
an1.249:1.1: His given name was Sudatta, but he is usually known by the sobriquet Anāthapiṇḍika, “feeder of the poor”. He features in countless discourses as the ideal of the generous lay follower.
an1.253:1.1: The Uggas were one of the leading _khattiya_ clans of Vesālī. Ugga’s giving is exemplified at [an5.44]().
an1.255:1.1: Of the same clan as Ambaṭṭha of [dn3]().
